sentences.text: CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJESH KUMAR
For the Petitioner : Mr. Abhishek Sriwastava, Adv.

For the State : Mr. Sardhu Mahto, A.P.P.
 ....
Heard learned counsel for the parties.

The applicant who is in custody since 11.10.2022 has approached this Court for grant of regular bail in connection with Pathrol P.S. Case No.95 of 2022, registered for the offence under Sections 376-DA, 323, 341 & 379 of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
It appears that the applicant is an accused of committing rape upon the victim girl aged about 15 years.
It has been submitted by learned counsel for the applicant(s) that complete set of F.I.R. alongwith its enclosure have been annexed with this bail application and there is no suppression on his part.
Innocence has been claimed by the learned counsel for the applicant and undertaking has been given for participation in the trial.

Further, it has been submitted that the FIR is against unknown but in the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C., she has taken the name of this applicant and it has been admitted that he knows her but in spite of it, he has not been named in the FIR.
There is improvement in the statement made by the victim.
There is no other corroborative evidence on record.
The address given by the informant is also found false during investigation.
Further, the investigation is complete.
On the above basis, prayer for bail has been made.
Learned A.P.P. has opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant.

Considering the above facts, the applicant, named above, is directed to be released on bail, on furnishing bail bond of Rs.10,000/-
(Rupees Ten Thousand Only) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Sessions Judge-III, Deoghar in connection with Pathrol P.S. Case No.95 of 2022,
Sajid Hussain @ Sajid Shekh vs The State Of Jharkhand ....
